page: Microsoft Azure HX176rs is a high-performance computing instance configured with 176 dedicated x86_64 virtual cores powered by Intel hardware under the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The architecture pairs this large core count with 1408 GB of system memory, delivering an 8 GB per vCPU ratio that accommodates substantial in-memory footprints and parallel computational execution without hardware accelerator dependencies.

Storage provisions for the instance include 4355 GB of integrated local NVMe SSD capacity alongside support for Azure Premium Storage. For inter-node communications across tightly coupled clusters, the platform features remote direct memory access (RDMA) capabilities, reducing network latency and overhead during distributed parallel computations.

From an infrastructure and resource density standpoint, the instance delivers a unified profile combining high compute density, substantial memory allocations, and fast ephemeral storage. Workloads that do not require GPU acceleration benefit from the dedicated CPU allocation and RDMA connectivity, making it suitable for distributed numerical simulations, high-performance computing (HPC), large-scale relational or in-memory databases, and batch analytics processing.
description: Microsoft Azure HX176rs is an x86_64 high-performance computing virtual machine offering 176 dedicated Intel vCPUs and 1408 GB of system memory, establishing an 8 GB per core memory footprint. Operating on Microsoft Hyper-V, the system integrates 4355 GB of local NVMe SSD ephemeral storage and provides native support for RDMA networking and Premium Storage volumes. With no GPU hardware present, this instance targets compute-dense and memory-intensive enterprise tasks. The combination of high core counts, large memory capacity, and low-latency RDMA inter-node communication makes the instance well matched for distributed scientific simulations, computer-aided engineering, memory-resident database management, and large-scale parallel processing workloads.
